value.part: The "massive Democratic wave" coverage is overblown
value.verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED. The early-vote wave is overblown; the Democratic environment is not
value.numbers: For: same 22 states, same day: D+14.7 now vs D+12.2 in 2022, a 2.5-point shift (+1.0 to +2.7 allowing a one-day alignment error), with the D share unchanged at 45.3 [M] (chk, R10). The big "wave" numbers use 2024: NBC/TargetSmart D+12 now vs D+2 at E-8 in 2024 [V] (R10). Volume is +30% on 2022 (26.55M vs 20.44M at E-10) [M][V] (R10), but early voting's share of the final vote rose from about 33% (2018) to 41% (2022) to 56% (2024) [V][M] (R10), so pace is not turnout. The Hill's "23M vs 15M" pairing implies +53%; the same instrument on the same day gives +31% [M] (R10). McDonald's "Republicans not as engaged" fails in Iowa (R ballots +26.8% vs D +14.6% on 2022) [M] (chk, R5). PA mail is 9.6 pts less D than 2022 [M] (chk, R3); NV is 2022 again (D+4.2 vs D+4.6) [M][R] (R8); WI returns are 10.4% below 2022 [R] (R5); SD 10.7% below [V] (R7). POLITICO: Democrats privately warn they may not reach their 2018 House seat total, 235 [V] (C3). Against: generic D+7.9 to D+10 on every average and no filter below D+5.7 [V][M] (C1, TX T101); Trump approval -21.6 (RCP) to -27.1 (FiftyPlusOne), and -32 in CNN's all-adult poll of polls [V] (C1); specials about 10 (median of the 2026 legislative specials) to 12.5 (The Downballot's mean for 2025-26) points better than Harris's 2024 margin, and in 2018 the specials also ran hotter than the November vote [M][V] (C4); real Democratic over-performance in NC (D+17.5 vs D+7.8 in 2022) [M] (chk, R1), MD in-person (D+36.4 vs D+23.5) [M] (R3), MN volume (+48.5%) [V] (R5), KS (volume x1.67, D in-person D+5.9) [M] (R7) and GA (Black share 33.0%, a five-cycle high) [R] (R1). Correct framing [I]: the media did not invent a wave; it measured the early vote against the wrong year.
value.caveat: Intellz read: the surge headlines measure against 2024, Republicans’ best early-vote year. Against the midterms, Texas is on the 2018 pace per registered voter and the 22-state party mix is flat with 2022. In our backtest of past state races the final polls missed toward Democrats by about 2 points on average, and the party-registration lead the media cites missed the result by 16.

value.numbers: For: in 2020 and 2022 the Democratic early margin shrank after E-10 (2022 D+12.2 to D+8.7, 2020 D+22.0 to D+14.3) [V] (R10); no same-state series exists to test 2018 or 2024. A 2022 replay ends the 2026 early vote at about D+11, a 2020 replay at D+7 [E] (R10). In 2022 early ballots were 46% of these states' vote; the rest came on or near Election Day [E] (R10). VoteHub's 9-state model: Democrats bank +367K, the remaining electorate is R by 1.79M, including 4.11M Republicans vs 2.56M Democrats who voted in all of the last three generals [V][E] (published / E model, R10). NC: 955,509 R-primary voters left vs 605,339 D, and equal tier turnout gives the 2022 mix (R+0.2 to R+0.5) [M][E] (R1). OH: affiliated remaining R +428k [E] (R6). Texas: Election Day ran redder than the early vote in 7 of 10 top statewide races since 2014 [M] (TX T93). Against: the gap between the final early-vote party margin and the House vote ran -2.6 (2018), +11.2 (2020), +11.4 (2022), +4.7 (2024) [V][M] (chk, R10). Applied to a projected D+7 to D+11 early vote, the 2020 and 2022 gaps imply a House vote of R+4.7 to D+1.1, the 2024 gap D+2 to D+6.5, and the 2018 gap, measured on its own 16 states, D+7 to D+12 [E] (R10). In 2018, the one prior Trump midterm, persuasion beat the late vote. In Nevada the lag is among Republicans who usually vote early, so "later" and "lower" cannot be told apart until Election Day [R] (R8).
